bright-angel-indian-garden.note: Bright Angel Trail is open from the trailhead to Mile-and-a-Half Resthouse; the trail remains closed from Mile-and-a-Half Resthouse to Havasupai Gardens, reconfirmed today on the park's Key Hiking Messages page (last updated October 15, 2026, unchanged since), which gives an expected reopening of Thursday, October 22, 2026 for this segment, combining the original August 29, 2026 flash flood damage with an October 13, 2026 rockfall; as of today, three days before that target, the segment has not yet reopened (Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park). The River Trail east of River Resthouse, plus Black Bridge and Silver Bridge, remain closed with no estimated reopening. Corridor water remains off at Havasupai Gardens, Three-Mile Resthouse, and Mile-and-a-Half Resthouse; it is available at the Bright Angel Trailhead tank. Confirm current conditions with the Backcountry Information Center at 928-638-7875 before descending past Mile-and-a-Half Resthouse. An NWS Flood Watch is in effect for the Grand Canyon Country/Kaibab Plateau area from Wednesday morning through Wednesday night, Oct 21-22 (Source: National Weather Service).

rim-trail.note: The Rim Trail and rim overlooks remain accessible per Grand Canyon's Key Hiking Messages page (last updated October 15, 2026, unchanged since), reconfirmed today, and are not affected by the Bright Angel Canyon flash flood closures, which are limited to inner-canyon corridor trails (Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park). An NWS Flood Watch is in effect for the Grand Canyon Country/Kaibab Plateau area from Wednesday morning through Wednesday night, Oct 21-22 (Source: National Weather Service). Use caution near the rim during any lightning.

north-kaibab-coconino.note: The entirety of North Kaibab Trail, from the North Kaibab Trailhead to Phantom Ranch, including Cottonwood Campground, remains closed following the flash flooding in Bright Angel Canyon on August 29, 2026 that destroyed footbridges and water pipeline infrastructure. The park's Key Hiking Messages page (last updated October 15, 2026, unchanged since), reconfirmed today, confirms the full closure and that Black Bridge and Silver Bridge river crossings remain closed, with no estimated reopening at this time (Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park). Phantom Ranch, Bright Angel Campground, and the Canteen remain fully closed as part of this closure. A separate Transcanyon Waterline construction closure between Redwall Bridge and Cottonwood Campground, effective October 15, 2026 through about February 2027 with no detour available, remains moot for through-hikers since this stretch is already closed due to flood damage. Corridor water remains off at the North Rim, North Kaibab Trailhead, Supai Tunnel, Manzanita Day Use Area, and Cottonwood Campground, with no restoration reported. An NWS Flood Watch is in effect for the Grand Canyon Country/Kaibab Plateau area from Wednesday morning through Wednesday night, Oct 21-22 (Source: National Weather Service).
